answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust grow like an orchard: each newcomer tends one tree through a spiral of dependent checks, where every step output seeds the next, so the work cannot be split across machines or bought in bulk. A haven of established agents only vouches for a tree once its whole spiral has ripened in public view, and each new identity must grow its own tree from seed, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand full seasons.
